items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: And it took all of us to keep Sam off of them when we got outside. Oh, Sam would have killed them both. They're both dead now. Willie Lewis and Herb Flemming.

ctx.x: Well, there were many. It's been 50 years -- 55 years ago and it's pretty hard for me to recall all of them. But I do remember a particular incident that happened while playing for an afternoon party for the queen of Spain. You know, she was English, she was married to King Alfonso, but she was English, very attractive, buxom blond, and we had been chosen to play this afternoon tea. There were a lot of British royalty there and Spanish royalty and dignitaries at this afternoon tea party. And we're playing -- let…

never got along. And this particular time the trombone player was standing up playing a solo and the saxophone player began to noodle in his solo and distract him. And they'd had this problem before, so the trombone player put his trombone down and walked over and squared off at the saxophone player. Well, we all jumped up to grab him so naturally the band stopped and the queen got up and put her to her eyes and she said, "My, my, what is going on?" And Sam -- we're all trying to separate these two guys in this…
But they did finish the engagement out for the Queen?
